title: Measuring Claim‑to‑Action Rates and Automated Defenses in Simulated Agentic NetOps Pipelines
abstract: We preregistered (hosted‑netops‑gvr‑v1‑2026‑08‑26) and executed a paired study that measures how often LLM‑produced configuration proposals would cause unsafe simulated deployments (claim→action or unsafe‑execution) and whether a guarded defense reduces that rate relative to an unguarded baseline. We generated 300 synthetic intent→configuration tasks and executed paired baseline and guarded conditions; 272 complete pairs were analyzable. On those 272 pairs the guarded pipeline actually executed in this run (deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared LLM generation; see Methods and Verified Deviation) produced baseline safe = 271/272 and guarded safe = 272/272, an absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281 (95% paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0). Provider‑call failures reduced the effective sample (28 failed hosted model calls). We report the preregistered conservative sensitivity treating failed episodes as unsafe (N=300): guarded safe = 272/300 = 0.9066666667; baseline safe = 271/300 = 0.9033333333; difference = 0.0033333333. All raw responses, provider traces, per‑episode scoring JSONs, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 checksums and manifest entries (paths and hashes cited in the Disclosure). We correct and document a verified execution deviation (the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed) and discuss implications for inference and operational measurement of defended agentic NetOps workflows.

sections.introduction: Automation that maps natural‑language intent to concrete network configuration changes can speed NetOps but also creates a concrete safety problem: fluent LLM outputs may propose valid‑looking commands that, when applied, violate reachability, isolate services, or otherwise break operational invariants. Engineering controls proposed across the literature include deterministic verification (reachability/policy checks), generate–validate–repair loops, multimodel consensus, and human gating. Prior work documents such controls separately, but few studies provide preregistered estimands, paired causal designs, and fully archived execution artifacts. Our study asks: in a deterministic simulator and under a preregistered paired design, what is the empirical claim→action (unsafe‑execution) rate for an LLM‑driven pipeline, and how much does a combined defense reduce that rate relative to an unguarded baseline? We preregistered the estimand and analysis plan, archived every model call and validator trace, executed the run, and report the executed results together with a verified execution deviation and sensitivity analyses.
sections.related_work: Deterministic validators and symbolic/SMT verifiers (NetKAT, header‑space, SMT‑based approaches) are established tools for operational correctness and form the technical baseline for validators used in defended agentic pipelines. Recent work on tool‑augmented LLM agents and generate–validate–repair architectures motivates multi‑stage defenses and ensemble strategies; agentic failure‑mode taxonomies highlight the claim→action gap when textual claims drive real actions. Our contribution is a preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired measurement of a guarded pipeline in a simulated NetOps setting, plus an explicit, verifiable record of an execution deviation that commonly arises in ensemble evaluations.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study preregistration (hosted‑netops‑gvr‑v1‑2026‑08‑26; preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe) specified a paired design with planned N=300 tasks (100 benign / 100 ambiguous / 100 adversarial). Primary estimand (explicit form used in all reported analyses):

  estimand = safe_rate_guarded − safe_rate_baseline

computed on complete paired outcomes. Here safe_rate_condition = (#pairs where validator marks configuration valid in that condition) / (#complete pairs). We use 'safe' to denote validator valid=true and 'unsafe' as valid=false; all text and tables follow this convention. Primary hypothesis H2 tested whether estimand>0. Analysis procedure: exact two‑sided McNemar on paired binary outcomes plus paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Preplanned conservative sensitivity ('failure_as_unsafe') treats episodes with failed model provider calls as unsafe for both conditions. Task generation and simulator. A deterministic task generator produced synthetic intent→configuration tasks each with initial state, required safe sequence constraints, and a deterministic reference configuration; the task manifest is archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl). For each task the pipeline produced one shared initial generation; baseline executed that generation directly through the deterministic validator; the preregistration had specified a guarded pipeline consisting of deterministic validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate. Execution logging and retrievability. We preserved every provider call trace, raw response, per‑episode scoring JSON, and validator_trace (paths and SHA‑256 values are listed in the execution manifest). Retry policy: one automatic retry on provider call failure; failed episodes post‑retries are logged and handled per the preregistered missingness plan. Verified deviation. Audit fields in the archived execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) show stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation":300,"repair":1} and condition_counts = {"shared":300,"guarded":1} indicating the preregistered ensemble stage (3‑model consensus) did not run; the guarded condition in this execution therefore equates to deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared LLM generation. This verified deviation is documented in the Disclosure and revises the inferential statement: the preregistered ensemble hypothesis was not tested in this run; instead the archived guarded comparison evaluates the alternate pipeline actually executed. Reproducibility. Minimal artifacts required to reproduce the primary contingency are archived and SHA‑256 hashed (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 682a629aee104ef5c3d3b3e494f881ca05fa38bc10831e1f7c9164c70c754c27; analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256 = b48494c4014de396afb395e78e227f827abc35f1777c23fa25b67b1d20d6f408; analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA‑256 = 97bde3aef2ce7228e290a8102ad97079586654c1fe512046d109268c93eae2c6; execution/execution_manifest.json lists every per‑file SHA‑256), enabling deterministic verification of all reported numbers from the archived run.
sections.results: Execution accounting and missingness. Planned episodes = 600; completed episodes = 544; failed episodes = 56 (execution/execution_manifest.json). Provider call audit: model_calls_used = 301; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28 (execution manifest). Complete analyzable pairs (both baseline and guarded outcomes present) = 272 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). Primary paired analysis (complete pairs N=272). The 2×2 contingency on complete pairs is: n11 = 271 (safe both baseline and guarded), n10 = 1 (safe baseline, unsafe guarded), n01 = 0 (unsafe baseline, safe guarded), n00 = 0 (unsafe both). Observed safe rates: baseline = 271/272 = 0.9963235294; guarded = 272/272 = 1.0. Absolute paired difference (safe_rate_guarded − safe_rate_baseline) = 0.003676470588235281. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Conservative preregistered sensitivity (failure_as_unsafe on planned N=300). Treating the 28 failed pairs as unsafe yields: baseline safe = 271/300 = 0.9033333333; guarded safe = 272/300 = 0.9066666667; guarded − baseline = 0.0033333333. Representative per‑episode artifacts. We publish representative per‑episode scored JSONs and raw responses; three examples are included in the archived manuscript evidence bundle (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json, task-000002-*.json, task-000003-*.json) and their SHA‑256s are recorded in the run manifest. Verified execution deviation and its effect on inference. The preregistered guarded design included a 3‑model consensus ensemble. The execution manifest shows that ensemble stage did not run; therefore the archived guarded result reports the validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared LLM generation (not the preregistered multimodel ensemble). Because the actual executed artifact differs from preregistration, claims about the preregistered ensemble must be deferred pending a re‑execution. All audit evidence proving this deviation is archived with per‑file SHA‑256s (see Disclosure).
sections.discussion: Practical interpretation. On the analyzable pairs the executed guarded pipeline (validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation) achieved near‑perfect acceptance, but the paired absolute improvement over baseline is extremely small (≈0.0037) and statistically inconclusive on the completed pairs (McNemar p = 1.0). The verified execution deviation prevents inferential claims about the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble. Operational lessons for measurement. (1) Provider reliability and orchestration matter: 28 failed hosted model calls reduced effective N and thus statistical power; robust retry/backoff, deterministic caching, and provider‑call accounting are prerequisites for ensemble evaluations. (2) Execution auditing must be built into preregistration: the runtime manifest must record per‑stage counts so a posterior audit can confirm the intended pipeline actually executed (we provide that audit evidence). (3) Deterministic validators remain a practical boundary: on our synthetic tasks the deterministic validator strongly enforces operational constraints and produces interpretable failure traces (validator_trace) that enable deterministic scoring; however, simulators and validators are approximations of device behavior and stateful interactions and must be treated as a construct validity limitation. Comparison with prior work. Our experiment operationalizes themes from LLM‑for‑NetOps and agentic agent safety literature: deterministic verification is useful in pipelines that translate intent→config, generate–validate–repair architectures are necessary, and ensemble defenses add operational complexity. Unlike many prior demos, we preregistered estimands, archived every artifact, and provide deterministic validator traces for each episode so others can reproduce the reported contingency counts. Limitations (artifact‑grounded). (i) Single declared model in artifacts (declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini") — no multi‑model generality claims. (ii) Synthetic tasks and a deterministic simulator — external validity to vendor devices and production environments is limited. (iii) Verified execution deviation — the preregistered ensemble was not executed; the run therefore evaluates a different defended pipeline than originally specified. (iv) Provider call failures (28 failed model calls) reduced the effective sample and thus power to detect small absolute effects. Recommendations. Future measurement runs should harden provider orchestration, re‑run the preregistered ensemble with seeded multi‑call traces, and expand simulator fidelity or move to controlled testbeds to probe external validity.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired study with full artifact archiving to quantify claim→action risk and to evaluate a guarded defense in a simulated NetOps setting. The run demonstrates the practical utility of deterministic validators for detecting unsafe proposed configurations and highlights three operational realities: provider‑call reliability materially affects evaluative power; ensemble defenses increase orchestration complexity and thus the risk of verified execution deviation; and deterministic per‑episode validator traces are essential for reproducible measurement. The preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed in this run (verified by the execution manifest); re‑execution with robust provider orchestration is required to evaluate that preregistered hypothesis. All per‑episode raw outputs, provider traces, per‑episode scoring JSONs, validator traces, and analysis files are archived with SHA‑256 checksums and are sufficient to reproduce the primary contingency and descriptive statistics (see Disclosure for minimal reproduction files and checksums). We release the archived artifacts so the community can reproduce, extend, and re‑execute the preregistered ensemble stage under hardened orchestration conditions for a definitive assessment of ensemble gains over validator+gate defenses.

disclosure_statement: Mandatory Disclosure Statement (CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track). Initial master prompt immutable reference (archived): provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Preregistration: hosted‑netops‑gvr‑v1‑2026‑08‑26; preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe (preregistration includes estimands, sampling plan, missingness and sensitivity plans). Declared model in archived execution artifacts: declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256 = 9b382b55079209fb91e16a8bc475265afc9496e07200d9d061c1a23d483523b2). Orchestration/adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (execution/execution_manifest.json lists this adapter and records full per‑file SHA‑256s). Deterministic validator used to produce safe/unsafe labels and validator_trace: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_id and validator_version appear in each execution/scoring/*.json). Preregistered guarded design: deterministic validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate (described in preregistration). Verified execution deviation: the ensemble (3‑model consensus) stage did not run in this archived execution (execution/execution_manifest.json audit fields stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation":300,"repair":1} and condition_counts = {"shared":300,"guarded":1}); the guarded condition archived therefore corresponds to deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared LLM generation (not the preregistered ensemble). The execution manifest and every per‑episode scoring JSON and response file are archived with SHA‑256s (see execution/execution_manifest.json for the full manifest). Human role: the Research Director selected the topic family and approved the master prompt prior to the autonomy lock. After the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature review, preregistration, task generation, code generation, model calls, validation, analysis, manuscript drafting, peer review, and revision without human manual editing of technical content, numbers, validator traces, or the Disclosure Statement. Reproducibility: minimal artifacts to reproduce the primary contingency and descriptive statistics are archived with SHA‑256s: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 682a629aee104ef5c3d3b3e494f881ca05fa38bc10831e1f7c9164c70c754c27), analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = b48494c4014de396afb395e78e227f827abc35f1777c23fa25b67b1d20d6f408), analysis/missingness_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 97bde3aef2ce7228e290a8102ad97079586654c1fe512046d109268c93eae2c6), execution/execution_manifest.json (full per‑file SHA‑256 manifest; example task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3d7b63c361c9848b20750cc44125f195f0341346d48393ce72ae07d6c0fea745). No human manual manuscript edits to technical content occurred after the autonomy lock. The run archive contains every raw provider trace and scoring JSON so all reported numbers are traceable to archived artifacts.
limitations: Single declared model present in artifacts (declared gpt‑5‑mini) — results do not generalize across model families or scales.
Synthetic intent→configuration tasks executed in an isolated deterministic simulator — construct and external validity are limited for vendor devices and production environments.

Verified execution deviation: the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed in this run; the archived guarded condition therefore evaluates validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation rather than the preregistered ensemble hypothesis.
Provider call failures reduced the effective sample: 28 failed hosted model calls (logged in execution audit) reduced the planned N and limit statistical power to detect small absolute effects.
